Questions,
answered.
faq.description: The things people ask before spinning up their first server. Need more detail?

location.question: Where do my apps actually run?
location.answer: On servers you own, in your own cloud account. launchctl provisions and operates them for you, but the infrastructure and data stay yours.

php.question: Can I run Laravel and PHP apps, not just Docker?
php.answer: Yes. Provision a server and deploy Laravel or any PHP app straight from Git — deploy scripts, environment, the scheduler and queue workers are set up for you. Docker apps, compose stacks and managed databases run alongside on the same platform.

queues.question: Can I monitor my queues?
queues.answer: Yes — watch queue workers, job throughput and failures live, and restart, pause or scale workers from the dashboard, with worker logs streamed in real time.

tokens.question: Do I need to manage GitHub tokens for CI/CD?
tokens.answer: No. We commit a managed GitHub Actions workflow that builds and pushes to GHCR, and mints a short-lived pull token per deploy — no long-lived PAT to set up or rotate.

workflow.question: Does committing the workflow trigger a deploy?
workflow.answer: Never. The workflow runs on workflow_dispatch only, so syncing the file or pushing code never auto-ships. Deploys are always explicit.

databases.question: Which databases are supported?
databases.answer: Managed PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB and Redis — each with scheduled S3 backups, one-click restore and connection details on tap.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.metaDescription: How launchctl (Gigcodes) collects, uses and protects your data. Your apps and data run on infrastructure you own.
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data launchctl collects, why, and the choices you have. launchctl is operated by Gigcodes (“we”, “us”).

who.heading: 1. Who we are
who.body: launchctl is a server-management and deployment platform operated by Gigcodes. We help you provision servers on your own cloud accounts and deploy and operate applications on them. This policy covers the launchctl website, dashboard and API.

collect.heading: 2. Information we collect
collect.accountBody: — your name, email address and a securely hashed password when you sign up, plus team membership details.
collect.billingBody: — subscriptions are processed by our payment provider, Polar. We receive your plan, subscription status and invoices, but we never see or store full card numbers.
collect.credentialsBody: — cloud-provider API tokens, SSH keys and connection details you add so we can provision and operate your servers. These are encrypted and used only to run the features you enable.
collect.usageBody: — logs, IP address, browser type and actions taken in the product, used to operate the service and debug issues.
collect.communicationsBody: — messages you send us via support or the contact form.

use.heading: 3. How we use your information
use.platform: To provide, operate and secure the launchctl platform.
use.billing: To process subscriptions, billing and refunds.
use.support: To provide support and respond to your requests.
use.reliability: To monitor reliability, prevent abuse and improve the product.
use.legal: To meet legal and regulatory obligations.
use.noSale: We do not sell your personal data, and we never have.

ownership.heading: 4. Your apps and data stay yours
ownership.body: The applications, databases and content you deploy run on servers in your own cloud accounts. We access your infrastructure only to perform the actions you ask of us — provisioning, deploying, streaming logs, running backups and similar. That data is yours, not ours.

share.heading: 5. Who we share it with
share.intro: We share data only with the providers needed to run the service:
share.connectedProviders: Cloud providers you connect (for example, DigitalOcean, Hetzner, AWS, Linode and Vultr) and GitHub for CI/CD, acting on your instructions.
share.infrastructure: Infrastructure and email providers we use to host launchctl and send transactional email.
share.authorities: Authorities, where required by law or to protect our rights and users.

retention.heading: 6. Data retention
retention.body: We keep your information for as long as your account is active. When you close your account or ask us to delete your data, we remove it within a reasonable period, except where we must retain certain records (for example, invoices) to meet legal obligations.

security.heading: 7. Security
security.body: We protect data in transit with TLS and encrypt sensitive secrets such as cloud tokens and SSH keys at rest. Access is restricted to what's needed to operate the service. No system is perfectly secure, but we work hard to keep yours safe.

rights.heading: 8. Your rights
rights.body: You can access, correct, export or delete your personal data at any time — from your account settings or by emailing us. We'll respond within a reasonable timeframe.

cookies.heading: 9. Cookies
cookies.body: We use essential cookies to keep you signed in and to remember preferences such as language and light/dark mode. We don't use them to track you across other sites.

changes.heading: 10. Changes to this policy
changes.body: We may update this policy from time to time. We'll revise the “last updated” date above and, for material changes, notify you in the product or by email.

refund.title: Refund Policy
refund.metaDescription: launchctl offers no-questions-asked refunds. Not happy in your first 30 days? Email us and we refund your subscription in full.
refund.intro: We keep this simple. If launchctl isn't working out for you, we'll refund you — no questions asked.
refund.leadBody: Within 30 days of any subscription payment, email us and we'll refund it in full — no forms, no hoops, no interrogation.

request.heading: How to request a refund
request.between: from the address on your account, or use our
request.afterForm: . Tell us which charge you'd like refunded — that's it. You don't need to give a reason.

covered.heading: What's covered
covered.subscription: Subscription payments billed by launchctl, refunded to your original payment method within 30 days of the charge.
covered.full: Refunds are issued in full — we don't pro-rate or deduct fees.
covered.effect: Once refunded, the related subscription ends and paid features switch off. Your servers and data are untouched — they live on your own cloud.

notCovered.heading: What we can't refund
notCovered.body: launchctl runs your apps on infrastructure you own, so charges from your cloud provider (such as DigitalOcean, Hetzner, AWS, Linode or Vultr) are billed directly by them, not by us. We can't refund those — please raise them with your provider.

beyond.heading: Beyond 30 days
beyond.body: Outside the 30-day window we're still happy to talk. You can cancel any time to stop future charges, and if something went genuinely wrong, reach out — we'll do the right thing.

questions.heading: Questions
questions.afterEmail: and usually reply within a business day.

terms.metaDescription: The terms that govern your use of launchctl, operated by Gigcodes — accounts, billing, acceptable use and your responsibilities.
terms.intro: These terms govern your use of launchctl, operated by Gigcodes. By creating an account or using the service, you agree to them.

service.heading: 1. The service
service.body: launchctl is a platform that provisions servers on cloud accounts you connect and helps you deploy and operate applications — Laravel and PHP apps, Docker stacks, managed databases and related tooling such as CI/CD, logs, queues, backups and SSL. We provide the control plane; the infrastructure runs on your own cloud.

account.age: You must be at least 16 and able to enter into a contract.

responsibilities.heading: 3. Your infrastructure and responsibilities
responsibilities.intro: Because your servers and applications run on cloud accounts you own, you are responsible for:

responsibilities.charges: Any charges your cloud provider bills you directly — these are separate from your launchctl subscription.

acceptable.malware: Host or distribute malware, or attack, probe or disrupt systems you don't own or aren't authorised to test.
acceptable.abuse: Interfere with or abuse the launchctl platform, or attempt to bypass its security or usage limits.

billing.heading: 5. Billing and subscriptions
billing.renewal: Paid plans are billed in advance through our payment provider, Polar, and renew automatically until cancelled.
billing.cancellation: You can cancel any time from your account; cancellation stops future charges and takes effect at the end of the current period.

thirdParty.body: launchctl works with services you connect, such as your cloud providers, GitHub and Polar. We're not responsible for those services or their availability, and your use of them is governed by their own terms.

ip.heading: 7. Intellectual property
ip.body: We own the launchctl platform, software and brand. You keep all rights to the applications, data and content you deploy. You grant us only the access needed to operate the features you enable.

Our total liability for any claim relating to the service is limited to the amount you paid us for it in the 12 months before the claim.

termination.body: You can stop using launchctl and close your account at any time. We may suspend or terminate access if you breach these terms or use the service in a way that risks harm to others or to the platform. Your servers and data remain on your own cloud.

changes.heading: 11. Changes
changes.body: We may update the service and these terms. We'll revise the “last updated” date above and, for material changes, give reasonable notice. Continuing to use launchctl after changes means you accept them.
